newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada manufacturers seek employment insurance cut.
newsitem.headline: Canada manufacturers seek employment insurance cut.

text.p: A leading Canadian business group wrote Prime Minister Jean Chretien on Thursday to push for a dramatic cut in unemployment insurance premiums in light of the insurance fund's big surplus.

The group, Alliance of Manufacturers & Exports Canada, advocated that the employees' premium, on which the employers' contribution is based, be cut to C$2.20 per C$100 of insurable earnings from C$2.90.
Finance Minister Paul Martin said in February that the premium would be cut to C$2.80 at the start of 1998, but has resisted pressure from the Reform and Conservative parties for a bigger cut.
The fund had a surplus of about C$8.6 billion at the end of May, a figure that will grow by C$500 million a month. The alliance said the total should not exceed C$5 billion.
Every 10-cent cut costs the government about C$600 million.
